newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi's Alujain says two copper projects on ice.
newsitem.headline: Saudi's Alujain says two copper projects on ice.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's Alujain Corp said on Tuesday it had put on ice two long-planned copper projects worth more than $600 million ahead of a government review of private-sector mining policy in the oil-rich kingdom.

"At present we are putting both projects on hold as a result of the government's intention to review its policy regarding mining activities by the private sector in Saudi Arabia," Alujain president Talal Bakr said in a written reply to questions from Reuters.
Bakr said another reason for the delay was "Alujain's inability to reach a suitable agreement with the Japanese partners for the development of the copper smelter".

Saudi Arabia is looking to develop its fledgling minerals sector as part of plans to diversify the oil-reliant economy. It has set up a committee to reassess previous mining practice and look at ways to encourage private investment in the sector.
Alujain had since 1993 planned to set up with a Japanese partner a $500 million smelter in Yanbu with an annual capacity of 150,000 tonnes of copper cathode.
Alujain has also been awaiting government approval for the development of the Jabal Sayid copper deposit northeast of Jeddah.

It has submitted two applications for an exploration licence -- one for an open-pit mine in partnership with Canada's Even Resources Ltd and the other for an underground mine with the Chinese state-owned China National Non-Ferrous Metals Industry Corp.
Development of the deposit was estimated to cost $100-200 million depending on the mining method chosen.
Alujain is a Jeddah-based joint stock company in which the Saudi Cable Co -- one of the country's largest private industrial firms -- is the biggest shareholder.
